transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Sylph SRE), Marcus Lane (Sylph CTO), Leah Ortiz (Sylph ML)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on latency/throughput for Sylph's clinical summarization and triage chat. Focus on p95 targets, concurrency, streaming token rates, and whether Hosted can meet requirements or needs Dedicated/Private.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side alex monroe, im the account lead, jordan is our systems engineer.
[00:12] Jordan (SE): hi all, jordan park here, i work on inference and perf at Redwood.
[00:18] Priya (SRE): hey, priya desai, i'm sres for sylph, thanks for making time. Marcus and Leah are on as well.
[00:26] Marcus (CTO): hi, thanks. short on time so appreciate a focused run.
[00:32] Alex: goal for today is to understand your p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming needs and what workloads you want us to run in a benchmark. also security and deployment constraints.
[00:44] Priya: cool. quick context: we run clinical note summarization plus a patient triage chat. summarization tends to be 500-1k tokens inputs, output 200-800 tokens. triage chat is stream-first, needs sub-second partial response for interactive feel.
[01:02] Leah (ML): we also have an embedding pipeline for similarity search for retrieval-augmented generation. embeddings are batched every 5 minutes, but embedding latency matters for pipeline throughput.
[01:15] Jordan: ok. rough q: target p95 for chat and for summarization?
[01:22] Priya: for chat p95 we'd like under 800ms end-to-end for short prompts (<=256 tokens) if we're streaming partial tokens; for full generation p95 for the whole response we'd accept up to 3s for 512-token outputs. summarization p95 ideally < 2.5s for 1k input -> 400 token output.
[01:46] Marcus: and concurrency, we expect spikes when clinics open, roughly 200 concurrent chat sessions, sustained 50-80 normally.
[01:55] Alex: got it. that 200 concurrency spike is helpful. one follow up: are you open to dedicated capacity or must be VPC/private due to PHI?
[02:06] Priya: we need SOC2, encryption-at-rest, and KMS integration; we prefer private or dedicated in a VPC for production. pilot can be hosted though.
[02:17] Jordan: perfect, we do SOC2 and have KMS integrations; for dedicated we can provision GPU pools and pin model versions.
[02:26] Alex: also curious about your token/sec expectations for streaming — do you have a target tokens/sec for throughput?
[02:33] Leah: for triage chat we want ~30-40 tokens/sec sustained per session for realtime feel; for bulk summarization it's more about tokens/sec at the cluster level, we need to process ~10k docs/hour during nightly runs.
[02:48] Jordan: ok that helps map to batching and quantization choices. in hosted we often recommend quantized variants for cost, but dedicated/private gives more kernel choice and can hit lower p95 with better hardware.
[03:01] Priya: can you explain the tradeoffs? especially p95 vs per-token cost.
[03:07] Jordan: sure. short version: lower latency usually means buying faster hardware or reducing batching. batching increases throughput and lowers cost per token but adds added latency variability — increases tail if queues form. dedicated lets you set concurrency and reduce queueing by reserving capacity. also caching prefixes helps for repeated prompts.
[03:24] Marcus: what's your approach to streaming? we need partial tokens pushed as they generate, and p95 should reflect user perceived latency for first token.
[03:33] Jordan: we support chunked streaming; for first-token p95 we optimize kernel selection and KV cache fetch. with dedicated and smaller batch windows you can get first-token p95 in low hundreds of ms on modern A100/H100 configs. hosted can achieve that too but depends on noisy neighbors unless you pick reserved capacity.
[03:51] Priya: noisy neighbors is a hard no for prod. for pilot we can tolerate, but prod needs isolation.
[03:57] Alex: noted. what about quantization — are you running int8 / 4-bit? and impact on generation quality for clinical content?
[04:06] Leah: quality is huge for clinical; we can't have hallucinations increase.
[04:10] Jordan: we have quantization profiles we recommend per-model. some 4-bit paths keep quality similar on most open models; we can run evals on your prompt set to measure regression. for clinical we usually suggest a conservative quantization profile and validate with your eval set.
[04:25] Priya: good. can you run a regression test?
[04:27] Jordan: yes, part of the pilot we run accuracy/regression vs your test prompts. we tie quality alerts to prompt sets in console.
[04:34] Marcus: for benchmarking, we need to know what you measure: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, tail latency per token, and resource utilization.
[04:43] Alex: exactly. our perf report includes p50/p90/p95/p99, median tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost-per-token estimates.
[04:51] Priya: what about concurrent request shaping — can you set max concurrent per model?
[04:57] Jordan: yes on Dedicated we expose concurrency and autoscale policies; you can configure max inflight per pod and maximum queueing latency. in hosted we have soft quotas.
[05:08] Leah: ok let's talk numbers — for the triage chat first token p95 under 800ms, sustained 30 tokens/sec per session, 200 concurrent spikes. can you map that to GPU requirements?
[05:19] Jordan: rough back-of-envelope: if you use a medium-sized decoder-only open model quantized to int8 on an H100, a single GPU can handle X sessions at Y tokens/sec — (note: numbers are illustrative) realistically for 200 concurrent you'll need a small pool of dedicated GPUs, or scale-out. for accurate mapping we need your exact model choice, sequence length distribution, and whether you need streaming at token-level or chunk-level.
[05:42] Priya: we're evaluating open models (Mistral / Llama-derivs) and considering a fine-tuned medical variant. we can share model and traces.
[05:50] Alex: please share traces and sample prompts — jordan will use them in the benchmarking script.
[05:56] Marcus: security: need SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS. can you integrate with our AWS KMS?
[06:04] Jordan: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys; we can integrate with AWS KMS and store audit logs in your syslog or forward via our SIEM integrations.
[06:12] Priya: retention policies?
[06:15] Alex: in Private/Dedicated you control retention. in hosted we have configurable retention windows, and we can sign BAAs and SOC2 docs. i'll send security pack.
[06:26] Leah: great. back to benchmarking: what does your token/sec benchmark look like?
[06:31] Jordan: we run synthetic and trace-driven runs. synthetic measures per-GPU token/sec at various sequence lengths and batch sizes; trace-driven replays your workload at target concurrency to produce p95/p99. we instrument with open telemetry for latency breakdown.
[06:45] Priya: timeline: we want pilot results in two weeks if possible.
[06:49] Alex: doable if we get traces and confirm schedules this week. jordan, can you estimate effort?
[06:55] Jordan: setting up the benchmark and run for two models typical takes about 2-3 engineer-days plus provisioning. if sylph provides traces and the prompt set today we'll be fine.
[07:07] Marcus: any preflight we need to do? network or IP allowlist?
[07:11] Jordan: for Dedicated/VPC we provide IPs and you can allowlist. for private on-prem we'll need network access and install windows.
[07:20] Priya: we will likely start with hosted pilot, then move to dedicated in staging. production to be VPC/dedicated.
[07:30] Alex: noted. question: do you need streaming chunk size tuning?
[07:33] Leah: yes we'd like chunk sizes tuned so first token is fast and the stream continues smoothly, without too many small payloads.
[07:41] Jordan: we tune max_final_token_buffer and stream frequency; smaller buffers give lower first token latency but increase server overhead. we usually recommend 20-40 token chunk sizes for triage chat.
[07:55] Priya: about cost, can you provide estimates for hosted vs dedicated assuming our nightly batch of 10k docs and 200 spike concurrency?
[08:03] Alex: we'll include a cost model in the pricing doc; brief note: dedicated has a higher fixed cost but predictable per-token cost and better tail latency. hosted is lower up-front but variable and might cost more under high sustained usage.
[08:17] Marcus: do you support warm KV cache across requests for repeated patient templates?
[08:21] Jordan: yes, we support prefix/KV caching, and caching-layer can be configured per-route. that helps reduce latency significantly for repeated contexts.
[08:30] Leah: how do you measure p95 for streaming vs non-streaming?
[08:34] Jordan: for streaming we measure first-byte p95 and token stepping p95 (time between emitted tokens). for non-streaming we measure end-to-end generation completion p95. both reported in the perf artifact.
[08:46] Alex: any regulatory concerns on model weights residency? some customers want weights in their VPC only.
[08:52] Priya: we would like weights not leaving our VPC for prod. is that supported?
[08:56] Jordan: in Private on-prem we can keep everything inside your network. Dedicated with VPC peering also keeps traffic in your private network and can be configured so that model artifacts are in your storage. we'll surface the options in the security pack.
[09:12] Marcus: ok, let's capture concrete next steps and owners.
[09:16] Alex: i'll recap at the end, but before that jordan, any questions about traces or the model?
[09:22] Jordan: just that we need a couple sample sessions that show worst-case lengths and average lengths, and embeddings batch file for the nightly run. also, if you have latency SLO doc specifying p95 vs p99 thresholds that helps.
[09:37] Priya: can do. i'll attach traces and a short requirements doc.
[09:41] Leah: also want to see how Redwood reports GPU proc utilization per request.
[09:46] Jordan: yes we include per-route GPU utilization and token-level time breakdown in the console and perf reports.
[09:55] Marcus: any blockers for pilot? licensing cost?
[09:59] Alex: we'll give a pilot pricing estimate; pilot can be time-limited with capped cost.
[10:05] Priya: solid.
[10:07] Alex: ok i'll do a quick recap and next steps.
[10:10] Alex: recap — Sylph wants: first-token p95 <800ms for chat; full generation p95 <3s for 512 tokens; summarization p95 <2.5s for 1k inputs. concurrency spikes ~200, steady 50-80. streaming at ~30-40 tokens/sec per session. security: SOC2, KMS, SSO; production in VPC/dedicated. Pilot: hosted ok. next steps: alex send security + pricing; jordan send benchmark script; priya share traces and p95 targets.
[10:39] Priya: that's right.
[10:41] Marcus: good. schedule pilot week of 2027-04-25.
[10:45] Alex: noted. thanks all.
[10:48] Leah: thanks.
[10:50] meeting ended
